clauses.reason: The order commands "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry" under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry; the approval has legal effect only through section 3 of that title (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: Complete operative inventory corrected from the provisional APP text: findings 1 to 5 are recitals that precede the command, and the only operative provision is the final approval of the code; the span runs from the second "Now, Therefore" to the end of that sentence.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6471A (signed December 2, 1933) first recites that the Secretary of Agriculture submitted the code and "do hereby find" five numbered findings (application made, notice given, hearings held, the code complies with section 3(a) clauses (1) and (2), and it will tend to effectuate the policy of Congress), then ends with the only command, "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry". The five findings are predicates of the approval, not commands. It states no period, condition, "until" date, exception or provisional approval, so no own-terms end applies. Under the reviewed shared analysis, the first end of such a command is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935) unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held for this code.

Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after the repeal.
